clue.text: Putting on part of "Aladdin" glitzily

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flashy, sequinned staging of the pantomime Aladdin.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a sum or extra amount is the everyday sense of totting or appending to it.

clue.text: Application for Nigel to get involved in a game of chance

indicators.note: in places the shuffled name inside the gambling game's word

parts.note: dice is the classic game of chance

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled together, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel is being asked to join a gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' looks like a form to fill in, but it means hard work; 'to get involved' turns NIGEL into LIGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is careful, sustained effort, which is what application to a task means.

clue.text: Light reveals sick bird looking up

parts.note: sick means ill

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means the bird's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A lamp shows a poorly bird gazing upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a verb here, and 'looking up' suits a down entry, read from the bottom; it turns EMU into UME.
explanation.definitionFit: Illume is a poetic verb meaning to light up or illuminate.

clue.text: A reason to corner the woodchuck

parts.note: a ground is a reason or basis, as in grounds for complaint
to hog something is to monopolise it, to corner the market in it

explanation.surface: Someone offers a motive for trapping a burrowing rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundhog is another name for the woodchuck, a North American marmot.

clue.text: Confusion is no good in a story

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the word for a story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A complaint that a muddled plot spoils a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a confused muddle or knot, so it is a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Revival of "Cats" includes nothing that's by Puccini

indicators.note: includes means the letter is taken inside the rearranged musical's name
a revival restages a show, so the musical's letters are put on in a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A theatre review notes that a new production of the musical Cats adds nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revival of' turns CATS into TSCA, and 'includes' puts O after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the famous 1900 opera composed by Giacomo Puccini.

clue.text: I turn ten chops, very healthy food

indicators.note: chops means cuts up, so the words are chopped and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook flips ten chops, a hearty and wholesome meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chops' reads as meat on the grill, but it is a verb telling you to chop up I TURN TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a nourishing substance in food, loosely described here as healthy food.

clue.text: Cavalry weapon used in combat originally in a way

indicators.note: in places the initial inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road

indicators.note: originally means only the starting letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier's weapon, first brought into battle long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes C from combat, and the second 'in' puts it inside LANE; the first 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lance is the long spear carried by mounted troops, the archetypal cavalry weapon.

clue.text: Italian scientist, one taking trail back to find Pope

indicators.note: back means the word for trail is read in reverse

parts.note: to lag is to trail behind
one is the Roman numeral I
Leo is a name taken by many popes

explanation.surface: An Italian scientist trudges back to meet the Pope, as Galileo was summoned to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAG into GAL, which the clue's 'one taking' puts in front of I; Galileo was famously summoned before the Pope's Inquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist tried by the Inquisition.

clue.text: Grand girl meets grand families in prisons

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
a lass is a girl
a great family or dynasty is a house, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A wealthy young woman marries into aristocratic dynasties within jails.
explanation.walkthrough: A glasshouse is British military slang for an army prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasshouse is military slang for a detention barracks, so glasshouses are prisons.

clue.text: As I can't move around, it's hellish

indicators.note: letters that move around change places, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in place complains that it is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means belonging to Satan, so devilish or hellish.

clue.text: In a vault I caught a friend in a mysterious fashion

parts.note: a crypt is an underground vault
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a burial vault with a companion speaks enigmatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptically means in an obscure or puzzling manner, a synonym for mysteriously.

clue.text: It makes my great-aunt evil in a quarrelsome way

indicators.note: makes says these words are made into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something turns a relative wicked and she becomes combative.
explanation.definitionFit: Argumentatively means in a disputatious manner, keen to argue, so quarrelsomely.

clue.text: Misbehave at the "King's Head" and disappear

parts.note: to sin is to misbehave

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone behaves badly at a pub called the King's Head and then vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name, here split into a word and its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to go under and vanish from view, hence to disappear.

clue.text: Activity of PM includes drinking

parts.note: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it means the afternoon: an afternoon social event where tea is drunk between dances

explanation.surface: Gossip that the Prime Minister's routine involves heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is post meridiem, the afternoon, and the drinking is of tea at a French-named tea dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A thé dansant is an afternoon tea dance, where tea is served between dances.

clue.text: Theatre where you could see Larry nude

indicators.note: you could see the letters in a new order, signalling an anagram of the name and word

explanation.surface: A risque production in which a man called Larry appears naked on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Drury Lane is a famous London West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, in London's West End is known simply as Drury Lane.

clue.text: Being pleased with a group of news gatherers demonstrating

parts.note: AP is the Associated Press, a news agency
proving means demonstrating, as in showing something true

explanation.surface: A satisfied press pack watches a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Approving of something means regarding it favourably, being pleased with it.

clue.text: Running time of "Cinderella"?

parts.note: not the length of a film or pantomime but the hour the heroine fled the ball as the clock struck twelve

explanation.walkthrough: Running time suggests a show's length; Cinderella literally ran from the ball at twelve o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, when Cinderella's spell broke and she ran off.

clue.text: Unfolding love to write down during a disorder

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to pen is to write down
in can mean during, as in in the night
gout is a painful joint disorder

explanation.surface: A love letter is written while the writer suffers an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening out means spreading or unfolding, as a map or flower does.

clue.text: It's about a hero getting a record 99

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
IC is 99 in a loose form of Roman numerals, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: A sporting hero scores a near-century of 99 and sets a record.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 99 is not strict Roman notation (that is XCIX) but crosswords allow it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem recounting the deeds of a heroic figure.

clue.text: Nimble appears in Act Four, beginning of end

parts.note: taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre note that a nimble character enters at the start of the closing scene of Act Four.
explanation.definitionFit: Active means energetic and lively, close in sense to nimble or agile.

clue.text: For teaching teenagers to back up a railway train

parts.note: to second a motion is to support or back it up
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Instructions on reversing a train along a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary school is where pupils of roughly eleven to eighteen are taught.

clue.text: Scold is veiled in church

indicators.note: in places the past-tense verb inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to veil is to hide, so veiled can mean hid

explanation.surface: A reprimand is concealed within a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to rebuke or tell off, a synonym for scold.

clue.text: Blushing after artificial insemination is made known

indicators.note: after means the colour word follows the abbreviation

parts.note: AI is the abbreviation for artificial insemination
blushing means going red

explanation.surface: Someone goes red once a fertility treatment is publicised.
explanation.definitionFit: Aired views are ones expressed publicly, so aired means made known.

clue.text: Chortle when Reginald has strong drinks to knock back

indicators.note: knock back suggests downing a drink but here reverses the run of letters

parts.note: Reg is a short form of Reginald
gins are strong drinks

explanation.surface: Reginald laughs as he downs several gins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock back' turns the whole run REGGINS round; the drinking sense is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A snigger is a smothered laugh, close in sense to a chortle.

explanation.definitionFit: Netted means caught or gained, as profit or fish brought in.

clue.text: Go greeny, which looks funny

indicators.note: a word that looks funny is distorted, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a greenish colour seems odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour or energy, as in full of go.
